minutes.headline: Select Board revised FY22 budget and capital articles for Town Meeting, but deferred a position on the $54,000 TCP design article.
minutes.summary: The finance director gave the third-quarter FY21 revenue and expense report, then the town manager walked through revised warrant articles ahead of Saturday's Town Meeting. The board recommended the revised prior-year expense, capital plan and omnibus budget articles, argued at length over the new TCP design article and deferred it, interviewed a registrar candidate, and approved minutes. It ended by entering executive session on collective bargaining.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to recommend the revised prior-year expense article, the revised capital plan article with changed funding sources, and the revised omnibus budget.
A motion to recommend Article 26, the TCP design fees, failed for lack of a second, and the board deferred its position until after the Article 25 presentation at Town Meeting.
The finance director gave the third-quarter FY21 report: local receipts ahead of estimate, interest income below it, no reserve fund draw, and a health insurance surplus expected.
The trash bid came in above estimate, so additional operating funds are covered by shifting capital funding sources.
The board appointed Karen Kemp to the Board of Registrars and will interview a second Republican nominee next week.

why_it_matters: The revised budget and capital articles are what residents will be asked to vote on at Saturday's Town Meeting, and the board's recommendations on them are now on the record.
Article 26 goes to Town Meeting without a Select Board recommendation, and a resident objected during public comment that no public hearing was held on the money.
watch_next: Town Meeting on Saturday, where the Article 25 presentation comes before the board gives its position on Article 26.
The board's interview of the second Republican registrar nominee next week.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the registrar appointment, Article 3, the omnibus total, the main budget figures and the Article 26 deferral. They differ on two things: our minutes record a capital plan vote that the official minutes do not, and they record Article 26 as a failed vote where the official minutes say the motion got no second and there was no vote. They also differ on whether Article 30 went on the consent calendar.
